title: Metaphor: ReFantazio Was Announced 8 Years Before It Came Out
hook:
Atlus announced Project Re Fantasy in December 2016, and it took almost eight years to become Metaphor: ReFantazio, which then sold 1 million copies on day one. Today it landed on Switch 2. Have you finished it, or is it still on your backlog?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Metaphor: ReFantazio was announced almost eight years before anyone could play it? In December two thousand sixteen, Atlus revealed a new team called Studio Zero. It was led by Katsura Hashino, the director of Persona five, and its first game had the working title Project Re Fantasy. Hashino said he wanted a role playing game rooted in traditional fantasy, a change of pace after years of Persona. Then the project went mostly quiet for a long time. The finished game finally arrived in October of two thousand twenty four with a brand new name, Metaphor: ReFantazio, and a very loud entrance. It sold one million copies on its first day, the fastest selling game in Atlus history. Two months later it won three trophies at The Game Awards: Best RPG, Best Narrative, and Best Art Direction. And this week the long road got one more stop. Today, November twelfth, the Switch 2 version of Metaphor: ReFantazio went on sale, five months after Atlus announced it during a Nintendo Direct. So a game that took the better part of a decade to make now fits in your hands. Have you finished the race for the crown, or is it still sitting on your backlog? Follow for more gaming history.
